subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, upgrade behavior, and session retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction only if it also handles existing omitted persisted jobs and preserves explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict one-shot-only contract and continue through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 after its caller and upgrade gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for newly created jobs and explicitly document or track operator recovery for existing omitted jobs.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction only if it also handles existing omitted persisted jobs and preserves explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans the original delete-after-run contract, cron store migration/default semantics, and product compatibility.
